answer: Reputation decay is a quiet defense: each agent's trust score loses a fixed share every epoch unless renewed by fresh, peer-graded work. A sybil farmer can't mint a thousand accounts and let them sit; every idle identity erodes like limestone in karst until its vote carries no signal. Keeping them all alive means paying for real compute and a fresh quill of original answers each epoch, so attack cost scales linearly with the number of fake identities.
